title: Weaver residual review session — residuals.json
description: Written by pack.py (via triage.py's build_residuals + cards.py's build_all_cards), read by the bound Copilot Chat agent and by draft_tier_b.py for any Tier B residual. MVP scope: derived from review-queue.json's own triggers (S1/S2/S5/low-architecture-coverage) — unmapped-signal-cluster catalogue_candidate promotion and generic ontology-conflict detection beyond S5 are named, real, separate extensions to this schema (real classes may be appended later; existing fields do not change shape). T-FS-1 (BACKLOG.md 'Tier-B residual detection') closed the prior 'no trigger produces tier B' gap: multi-hop-single-candidate-below-threshold (multi-hop-bridge-detector.ts's tier-b-single-candidate ignored-item, a single real store candidate found among a bridge's several syntactic implementers) now maps to tier 'B'.

id.description: Stable within one Session Pack; not reused across packs.

tier.description: A = architect must decide (choice card). B = LLM may draft if evidence bar met (either in-chat via Copilot's editFiles tool, the primary path, or the secondary/headless draft_tier_b.py; T-FS-1's multi-hop-single-candidate-below-threshold trigger is the first real producer of this tier). C = do not invent; document OOS or leave open.

card.description: Deterministic markdown choice card (cards.py) — options from a fixed per-class generator, an evidence blockquote, and a similar-residuals note. For a carried_forward residual this is a short note instead of a full card. This is the field the bound chat-mode agent presents as-is; it does not re-derive or invent options from the other fields.

class.description: One of Architect_Residual_Review_Session.md §3's taxonomy classes, e.g. multi-candidate-bridge, security-authority-policy, ontology-judgment, missing-intermediates-not-in-scan. Not a closed enum in this schema — new trigger->class mappings are additive in triage.py, same discipline as signal-catalogue.yml.

trigger.description: The originating review-queue.json trigger (or, for future non-review-queue sources like unmapped clusters, a distinct source tag) — always traceable to a real, computed signal, never invented.

unitIds.description: Empty for a genuinely run-level residual (e.g. S5-cfn-routes-found-but-unbound) — by definition no unit was matched, so none can be named. Never fabricated to fill this field.

evidenceRefs.description: file:line refs, each expected to have a corresponding redacted snippet in evidence/packs.json.

status.description: 'carried_forward' is set by pack.py --baseline when a prior session already decided this exact residual — never re-carded. 'drafted'/'applied' are not yet set by any built tool (no code path marks a residual resolved after apply — see the effective_ir.py MVP's own honest note about this).

reconfirm.description: (--baseline). True when a prior session's decision exists for this residual's unit, but THIS run's (trigger, class) differs from what the baseline recorded — the underlying source/facts likely changed shape since the decision was made. Never silently carried forward or silently overwritten; still gets a real, fresh choice card. Absent (not false) when no baseline was given or no prior decision matched.

consequence.description: T-RT-2 (BACKLOG.md 'Consequence-ranked queue'). Written by consequence.py's annotate_residuals(), read by queue_rank.py to sort the backlog highest-consequence-first. 'pii-proxy'/'external-system-identity'/'trust-boundary-edge' are named proxies for real, already-computed facts (TypedUnit.kind, TypedRelationship.kind) — see consequence.py's own module docstring for the exact mapping and its honest limits (this pipeline has no real PII/data-classification detector).
